title: RiskCueBench: Benchmarking Anticipatory Reasoning from Early Risk Cues in Video-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2601.03369v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: With the rapid growth of video centered social media, the ability to anticipate risky events from visual data is a promising direction for ensuring public safety and preventing real world accidents. Prior work has extensively studied supervised video risk assessment across domains such as driving, protests, and natural disasters. However, many existing datasets provide models with access to the full video sequence, including the accident itself, which substantially reduces the difficulty of the task. To better reflect real world conditions, we introduce a new video understanding benchmark RiskCueBench in which videos are carefully annotated to identify a risk signal clip, defined as the earliest moment that indicates a potential safety concern. translated_title: RiskCueBench：基于早期风险线索的视频-语言模型前瞻性推理基准测试
translated_abstract: 随着以视频为中心的社交媒体的快速发展，从视觉数据中预测风险事件的能力是确保公共安全和预防现实世界事故的一个有前景的方向。先前的工作已经在驾驶、抗议活动和自然灾害等领域广泛研究了有监督的视频风险评估。然而，许多现有数据集为模型提供了完整的视频序列（包括事故本身），这大大降低了任务的难度。为了更好地反映现实世界的情况，我们引入了一个新的视频理解基准RiskCueBench，其中的视频经过精心标注以识别风险信号片段，即指示潜在安全隐患的最早时刻。实验结果表明，当前系统在解读不断演变的情境以及根据早期视觉信号预测未来风险事件方面存在显著差距，凸显了……
tldr: 该论文提出了RiskCueBench基准，通过标注视频中最早出现风险信号的时刻，评估视频-语言模型仅凭早期视觉线索预判未来危险事件的能力，实验发现现有系统的前瞻性风险推理能力仍存在显著不足。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces RiskCueBench, a new video understanding benchmark that annotates the earliest risk signal clips in videos to evaluate video-language models' ability to anticipate future risky events from early visual cues, revealing a significant gap in current systems' anticipatory risk reasoning capabilities.
